definitions.explanation: The number one when counting small objects or general items.
Used in casual speech to indicate age difference.

examples.japanese: りんごを{一個|いっこ}ください。
{一個|いっこ}100{円|えん}で{売|う}っている。
examples.english: They're selling them for 100 yen each.

examples.japanese: ここに{一個|いっこ}だけ{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.english: There was only one left here.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{一個|いっこ}{上|うえ}だ。
{一個|いっこ}{下|した}の{後輩|こうはい}がいる。
examples.english: I have a junior who's one year younger.

examples.japanese: {一個|いっこ}{違|ちが}いなので{気|き}が{合|あ}う。
examples.english: We get along because we're only one year apart.

notes:
{一個|いっこ} is a very common counter for objects.

SENSE 1 - COUNTING OBJECTS:
- {卵|たまご}{一個|いっこ}: one egg
- {一個|いっこ}ずつ: one at a time
- {一個|いっこ}{単位|たんい}: per piece

SENSE 2 - AGE DIFFERENCE (CASUAL):
- {一個|いっこ}{上|うえ}: one year older
- {一個|いっこ}{下|した}: one year younger
- {二個|にこ}{上|うえ}: two years older

COUNTING:
- {一個|いっこ}、{二個|にこ}、{三個|さんこ}...
- {個|こ} is one of the most versatile counters in Japanese

NOTE:
The age difference usage ({一個|いっこ}{上|うえ}/{下|した}) is casual/colloquial.
